title: California statewide just cause for termination of tenancy
requirement: After 12 months of continuous lawful occupancy an owner may not terminate a residential tenancy without just cause stated in the written notice, and only for the at-fault or no-fault causes listed in the section.
coverage_conditions: Residential real property, including mobilehome tenancies and units in mobilehome parks, after 12 months of continuous lawful occupation by the tenant, or 24 months for one tenant.
exemptions: Transient hotel occupancy; dormitories; housing where the tenant shares a bathroom or kitchen with an owner-occupant; single-family owner-occupied residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplexes; housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; separately alienable homes with required notice; deed-restricted affordable housing.
penalty: Noncompliance voids the written termination notice; an owner who materially violates the section is liable for actual damages, attorney’s fees and costs, and up to three times actual damages for willful conduct, and the Attorney General or local city attorney or county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
interaction: Yields to a more protective local just cause ordinance adopted or amended after September 1, 2019; a property is not subject to both.

title: Relocation assistance or rent waiver for no-fault just cause termination
requirement: For a no-fault just cause termination the owner must, regardless of the tenant’s income, either pay one month’s rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month’s rent, and must advise the tenant of that right in the termination notice.
coverage_conditions: Any tenancy that requires just cause to terminate under subdivision (a) where the owner issues a termination notice based on a no-fault just cause, regardless of the tenant’s income.
exemptions: A tenant found at fault for the condition triggering a government agency or court vacate order is not entitled to relocation assistance.
penalty: Failure to strictly comply with the subdivision renders the notice of termination void; relocation assistance actually paid is recoverable as damages in an action to recover possession.
citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2: relocation assistance or rent waiver for no-fault just cause
quoted_span: (3) (A) The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy. Any relocation assistance shall be provided within 15 calendar days of service of the notice.
interaction: Any relocation assistance or rent waiver is credited against relocation assistance required by any other law.

note: Continuation of Civ. Code § 1946.2; its rules were recorded from part 1 D023-01.

title: Tenant Protection Act annual rent increase cap
requirement: An owner may not increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or unit by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period.
coverage_conditions: Residential real property, including dwellings and units in mobilehome parks, subject to subdivision (a); a new tenancy’s initial rent is set freely, with the cap applying only to later increases.
exemptions: Deed-restricted affordable housing; dormitories; housing under public rent or price control with lower annual increases; housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; separately alienable homes owned by natural persons with written notice; owner-occupied duplexes.
penalty: An owner who demands, accepts, receives or retains rent above the maximum is liable for injunctive relief, the amount of the overcharge, attorney’s fees and costs, and up to three times the overcharge for willful conduct; the Attorney General and local counsel may enforce.
quoted_span: (a) (1) Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
interaction: Does not authorize local rent increase limits beyond Chapter 2.7 and does not affect local authority to adopt or maintain rent control.
conflict_note: Subdivision (h) applies the cap to increases occurring on or after March 15, 2019, while subdivision (n) states the section became operative April 1, 2024.

title: Limit of two rent increases in any 12-month period
requirement: If the same tenant remains in occupancy over a 12-month period, the owner may not increase the gross rental rate for that unit in more than two increments during that period.
coverage_conditions: A unit of residential real property where the same tenant remains in lawful occupancy over any 12-month period, subject to the other restrictions of subdivision (a).
exemptions: Does not restrict the initial rental rate established for a new tenancy in which no tenant from the prior tenancy remains in lawful possession.
penalty: An owner who demands, accepts, receives or retains rent above the maximum allowed is liable for injunctive relief, the amount of the overcharge, attorney’s fees and costs, and up to three times the overcharge for willful conduct.
citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12: no more than two increases in 12 months
quoted_span: (2) If the same tenant remains in occupancy of a unit of residential real property over any 12-month period, the gross rental rate for the unit of residential real property shall not be increased in more than two increments over that 12-month period, subject to the other restrictions of this subdivision governing gross rental rate increase.
